outcome.technical: plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py: (1) _scan_quotes now delegates to a new _scan_contexts, which also returns where each open context began (one scanner, so marker quoting and enclosing substitution cannot disagree). (2) New _substitution_runs_body(prefix, cmd): when the marker sits inside a $( ), the head is read from the INNERMOST substitution (_head_runs_body on the text after its $( ); if that head runs its stdin it answers; otherwise the body is the substitution's output and stays data only when exactly one substitution is open, it is the whole of one double-quoted argument, the enclosing command is not in command position (empty, or after ; & | ( newline), and _holds_output_as_text vouches for the consumer: a plain script run (no interpreter env option such as NODE_OPTIONS anywhere in the command) or git commit/tag with the substitution as a -m/--message value (_GIT_MESSAGE_OPTIONS). Everything else returns shell. Returns False when no substitution is open, and split_heredocs then reads the marker line's head as before. split_heredocs builds the prefix from the kept lines plus the marker line, so a $( opened on an earlier line is seen too (before, `bash -c "$(` + newline + `cat <<'EOF'` dropped its body as data). (3) _last_command returns shell_words of the last simple command (falls back to a blank split when quoting never closes), and _pipes_to_script_run reads the far side with shell_words, so a quoted script path no longer disqualifies a plain script run; _plain_script_run's char check is unchanged and now applies to dequoted words. Docstrings of _plain_script_run, _last_command and split_heredocs updated. tests/test__config.py: new _house_body_cases (hb1-hb5) wired into _all_cases. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: a paragraph under the _config.py section on the shared heredoc split's substitution reading. UNDECLARED FILE CHANGED: tests/test_guard_history_rewrite.py (the plan gate allowed the Edit, no refusal): gw14e and gw14d pinned the defect - the house commit form's body graded as shell so its apostrophe made the amend's directory unknown. Both now use `$(bash ./msg <<'EOF'` (a substitution whose own head is a shell), keeping the unknown-directory property; new gw14i asserts the house form in the main checkout is allowed (the body is data). Without that change the suite reads 289/291 (gw14d, gw14e) against 291/291 at HEAD (git archive HEAD export). Mutation table run in a scratch copy, never the shared tree: consumer always text -> hb4 red; substitution always shell -> hb1 hb2 hb3 hb5 red; no dequote in _last_command -> hb5 red; interpreter-env check dropped -> hb4 red; command-position check dropped -> hb4 red; innermost head ignored -> hb4 red; pipe far side raw split -> hb5 red; each restored. Commands, all exit 0: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__config.py (375 cases); sweep over tests/test_guard_history_rewrite.py tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py tests/test__output_lints.py tests/test__deps.py tests/test__refs.py (5/5, 1718 cases); sweep over .claude/hooks/guard-release.py guard-uncommitted.py require-claim-block.py (3/3, 195 cases); ruff check and vermin -t=3.8- on the three .py files; python3 tools/bench-hooks.py --gate (10 hooks within budget, measured on 3.14 only - 3.8-3.13 not measured, no interpreter here). tools/prove-gates.py has no row anchored in _config.py (grep for _config.py there finds only prose), so no row needed changing. Left for the register (not fixed, outside scope): (a) _STDIN_SHELL's `\bsh\b` matches a script FILE extension, so `"$(cat foo.sh <<'EOF'` or `x.sh` in a head grades its body as shell (found when a hb4 fixture `bash x.sh` was caught by it instead of by the new code); (b) _scan_quotes tracks no backquote substitution, so a house form spelled with backquotes inside double quotes opens no heredoc at all and its body lines stay command text; (c) `gh pr create --body "$(cat <<'EOF'` is not a vouched consumer and its body still grades as shell (a deliberate allow-list limit).
